course_title: Undergraduate Research in Economics: ATL Economics
subject: ECON
course_description: Students will learn the craft of research in economics. Coursework will consist of synthesis of literature; collection, collation, cleaning of data; data analysis, contributing to manuscript preparation, and/or other work related to the sustaining of an academic research project.
course_notes: ATL Economics: Past, Present, and Future uses Atlanta to teach students how economists research and try to solve real-world problems. This course is organized as a research seminar. It uses Atlanta as a living laboratory for the study of urban economics, inequality, mobility, housing, education, infrastructure, finance, governance, and economic development. The course uses a blend of independent research and group-based study, with a methodological mix of historical/institutional analysis and statistical applications. Students will work in research teams throughout the semester to identify an original economics question, locate scholarly sources, build a research design, and produce a policy-relevant or academic research final project. Class time will be used for short framing discussions, methods workshops, data sessions, research-group consultations and updates, site visits, and discussions with invited guests. A key feature of the course will be learning to employ AI tools appropriately and efficiently to accelerate research productivity while maintaining the highest academic and intellectual standards.
